subject: Chemistry
topic: Potassium permanganate: preparation and oxidising action
title: The Mineral Chameleon: Potassium Permanganate
summary: Potassium permanganate is made by fusing pyrolusite (MnO₂) with KOH and an oxidiser to give dark green potassium manganate (Mn +6). In neutral or acidic water manganate disproportionates (3MnO₄²⁻ + 4H⁺ → 2MnO₄⁻ + MnO₂ + 2H₂O), the 'mineral chameleon' Glauber saw; commercially it is oxidised at an anode. In acid MnO₄⁻ takes 5 electrons to give almost colourless Mn²⁺ (so it is its own indicator in titrations); in neutral or faintly alkaline solution it takes 3 electrons and gives brown MnO₂.

notes.title: 15 – Potassium Permanganate: Preparation and Oxidising Action

keyPoints: Acid: **MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O**; purple → almost colourless, a **self-indicator**.
Neutral / faintly alkaline: **3e⁻ → brown MnO₂**. The medium decides the product.

blocks.p: 5Fe²⁺ + MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O + 5Fe³⁺. 0.02 mol MnO₄⁻ oxidises 0.10 mol Fe²⁺. The end point is the first permanent pale pink.
